strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout via cartTotal() in src/cart.js: a 10% bulk discount for 10+ items (summed over line quantities), the SAVE5 coupon ($5 off after the bulk discount, floored at $0, other codes refused), and $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods reach $50 (empty cart is free). Unit tests in Vitest prove each rule and its boundaries through the public cartTotal function, importing the thresholds from the code. Reading the code shows bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount — contrary to AC1 and to the function's own doc comment ("at least this many"); that case will be kept as an expected failure and reported as a defect.
inScope: cartTotal() in src/cart.js: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, unknown coupon refusal, shipping threshold, empty cart
Boundaries: exactly 10 / 9 items, goods exactly $50 / $49.99, goods floored at $0
outOfScope: Any UI or API checkout flow (the repo is a pure pricing library)
assumptions: Prices and the result are dollars as numbers rounded to cents by the module, so toBe on the expected rounded value is exact.
'Refused with an error' means cartTotal throws; the test checks the thrown message names the code submitted (the part the test controls).
Coupon codes are case-sensitive: 'save5' is a different code and is refused (the ticket says any other code is refused).
A non-empty cart whose goods drop to $0 through the coupon still pays $4.99 shipping, as AC3 says shipping is $4.99 whenever goods are under $50 and only an empty cart costs nothing.
openQuestions: Should a non-empty cart that a coupon brings to $0 still pay $4.99 shipping? The code and AC3's wording say yes; the tests assert that.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold: the code uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so exactly 10 items get no discount.
risks.mitigation: TC2 asserts the discount at exactly 10 items (expected failure, defect recorded); TC1/TC3 pin 11 and 9 items.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount would change the bulk amount.
risks.mitigation: TC4 uses a cart where the two orders give different totals (103 vs 103.5).

risks.description: Shipping judged on the pre-discount subtotal, or goods going negative.
risks.mitigation: TC5 and TC10 pick carts where the wrong order or no floor gives a different total.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, the goods never cost less than $0, and any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs nothing.

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart whose line quantities add up to more than 10
testCases.rationale: Proves quantities across lines are summed and the 10% applies.

testCases.title: gives 10% off a cart of exactly 10 items
testCases.expected: 90; the code returns 100 (uses > instead of >=), so the test is marked expected-to-fail and a defect recorded
testCases.rationale: Boundary named by the ticket ('10 or more').

takes $5 off with SAVE5 after the bulk discount
never lets SAVE5 take the goods below $0
testCases.expected: 4.99 (goods $0 plus shipping); without the floor it would be 2.99

testCases.title: refuses an unknown coupon code with an error
testCases.expected: throws an Error whose message names SAVE10

testCases.title: refuses a coupon code that differs from SAVE5 only in case
testCases.expected: throws an Error whose message names save5
testCases.rationale: Any other code, including near-matches, is refused.

testCases.title: ships free when the goods cost exactly $50
charges $4.99 shipping when the goods cost $49.99
judges free shipping on the goods after discounts
testCases.expected: 53.99 (49 + 4.99); judging on the subtotal would give 49

testCases.title: charges nothing for an empty cart
charges nothing for an empty cart with SAVE5
testCases.rationale: Coupon on an empty cart must not go negative or add shipping.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total gets 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD` (BULK_THRESHOLD = 10), so a 10-item cart pays full price. Its own doc comment says "at least this many". Expected `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) returns 100, expected 90; the test is marked it.fails and the counted run confirms it fails as expected.
